figures.caption: Figure 13.1.1 shows the chip architecture to efﬁciently conﬁgure the major changes in GDDR7 SDRAM. The system-level conﬁguration halves the CA pins from 10 to 5, while doubling the baud rate, which increases transmission efﬁciency, in terms of power and signal integrity. The staggered PAD structure is also used to minimize the path of the on-chip clock-distribution network (CDN) and to improve insertion loss and crosstalk. The CA RX clustered near the border of the CA and data peripheries, mitigates the pinto-pin skew and phase mismatch of the frequency-divided WCK, which must be transferred from the data periphery due to the absence of the command clock. Newly introduced features, such as PAM3 encoding/decoding, data scrambling, and ECC, as well as the doubling of internal processing data, contribute to GDDR7’s power increase. To power-efﬁciently achieve a high-speed column-to-column access of less than 1ns, all functional blocks are evenly distributed in the area where the internal data bus passes from the bank to the data periphery and are conﬁgured as signal repeaters to optimize logic delay and power.

A C2C, with a capacitor, uses direct-bridge control to ensure faster DC-convergence time for the following node (A), than the resistor-feedback path in Fig. 13.1.2.
